subject: Observability & Eval Playbook — follow-up and technical deep-dive
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Observability & Eval Playbook — follow-up and technical deep-dive

Hi Sophie — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. I pasted a short TL;DR of pain, goals, and the immediate ask below.

TL;DR:
- Pain: unpredictable production regressions after model updates; no signal for prompt-level regressions; limited request tracing into model versions; dashboards are ad-hoc and not tied to golden prompts.
- Current stack: you mentioned using SageMaker endpoints for hosted models, an in-house Redis cache for prefixes, and a homegrown metrics pipeline (Prometheus -> Grafana).
- Success criteria (what would make this a win for Fintegrate): 1) detect regressions automatically on deploy, 2) per-route dashboards with golden-prompt baselines, 3) tracing hooks from request -> model variant -> KV cache hit, and 4) rollout guardrails (canary + automatic fallback) with SLOs for p95 latency and per-token cost targets.

What Redwood will deliver for the POC (proposed):
1) Observability playbook PDF with example dashboards (error/quality/latency/cost) and alert thresholds (attached: observability-evals-playbook-v1.pdf).
2) Golden prompt set template + example spreadsheet we can use to run evals (attached: golden-prompts.xlsx).
3) Tracing hooks + instrumentation checklist we can add to your proxy layer (we can provide a small middleware snippet).
4) Regression alert config and a rollout guardrail plan (canary metrics, rollback triggers, fallback to smaller model variant).

Immediate asks from Fintegrate:
- Share a representative set of 50–100 golden prompts (or a sample CSV) and one recent deployment log with model version tags.
- Confirm whether you want the playbook scoped to your existing Grafana stack or if we should propose Redwood Console templates.
- Time preference for a 60m technical deep-dive (engineers + infra) next week — I proposed a few slots in the calendar link below.

Next steps I propose:
1) You drop the sample prompt CSV + sample logs to the HubSpot record or reply with a Drive link.
2) We schedule the deep-dive (Neha will lead the instrumentation portion).
3) Redwood will deliver the playbook & golden prompt baseline within 3 business days after we receive the samples.

Attachments: observability-evals-playbook-v1.pdf (playbook), golden-prompts.xlsx (template).

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly.

—
Camila Reyes
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

2) Grafana: we'd prefer to keep the dashboards in Grafana for now (security/approval path is faster). Please include Grafana JSON templates if possible.

Hi Sophie / team — Neha from Redwood's Applied ML / Observability team here. Short technical note on what we'll prepare for the POC and the minimal instrumentation we need from Fintegrate.

What Redwood will ship for the POC (deliverables):
- Grafana dashboard JSONs: latency (p50/p95/p99), token-cost, error-rate (by route), golden-prompt baseline panel (compare current vs baseline quality metric).
- Tracing hooks: small middleware (Node/Python) that emits trace id, request id, model_version, kv_cache_hit boolean. These are lightweight headers we can plumb into your proxy.
- Eval runner config: We will run the golden prompts against the candidate model(s) and produce a regression report (delta vs baseline) with suggested thresholds for automated alerts.
- Rollout guardrails: canary window config, metric thresholds (quality delta > 2% over baseline or latency p95 increase > 30% triggers rollback), and automatic fallback to a pinned variant.

Minimal data we need from you to execute quickly:
1) Sample prompt CSV (50–100 rows) and labeling guidance (what "good" looks like).
2) Last two weeks of request logs with model_version tag (or a 24h sample) — scrub PII before sharing.
3) Grafana access (read-only) or a JSON export so we can import templates directly.

Rough timeline once we have samples / access: 72 business hours to deliver draft dashboards + regression report. We'll keep the run reproducible and attach the eval configs so you can re-run in future.

Camila — I can lead the technical session and bring a short demo of the tracing middleware. If Sophie prefers Tue 6/22 at 10:00 PT, I can pencil that in.

—
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Observability | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
